recipes.name: Savory Cheddar Zucchini Muffins
ingredients_raw: 4 slices bacon, cooked crisp and crumbled

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 12-cup muffin tin or line cups with paper liners.
Combine flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a bowl.

Stir milk, zucchini, butter, egg, and garlic together in a separate bowl until well blended. Mix flour mixture into milk mixture, ½ cup at a time, stirring well after each addition, until the flour mixture is incorporated. Fold in Cheddar, Parmesan, and crumbled bacon: pour batter into the prepared muffin cups.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center of a muffin comes out clean, 30 to 35 minutes. Cool slightly before removing from muffin cups. Serve warm; refrigerate leftovers.

raw_recipe.headline: Savory Cheddar Zucchini Muffins
raw_recipe.description: This breakfast-friendly savory Cheddar zucchini muffin recipe features Parmesan for extra cheesy flavor and crispy bacon for a salty, crunchy bite.

review.reviewBody: I am the submitter of this recipe. I have just made another batch after receiving a less than stellar review. I followed the recipe exactly and had excellent results, again. My total baking time was 32 minutes. Some pointers to follow when baking anything - allow cold ingredients to come to room temperature (unless the recipe specifically states COLD). Cold ingredients drop the temperature of the batter resulting in longer baking time/underdone baked goods. This recipe calls for milk and an egg. I let mine warm up first (you can cheat here). Remember that oven temperatures vary, but the temp is always hotter at the top and cooler at the bottom. Opening the oven door repeatedly can also drop the temperature by up to 25 degrees. I do have one recommendation - if you use liners, I'd go with the foil type - the cheese in these muffins tends to stick to the paper. These are a moist muffin inside - there is yummy melty cheese all through.

These buscuits are so tasty!! They are definitely not bland, but packed with flavor! I used fresh home-grown zucchini, fresh fried bacon, shredded cheese, and freshly crushed garlic. Anything else added would be too much. I put mine in cupcake wrappers and were done in about 15-20 minutes. Moist and delicious! Thanks for the awesome recipe!

I just tried this recipe and they are really good! I saw some of the comments and had updated the recipe to use old cheddar and 6 slices of bacon. I thought I had 2 cups of zucchini, but after I froze it, thawed and drained the water, it looked more like 1 cup, but I was preparing double the recipe, so this will have a factor in the moisture. Mine doubled in size after baking and to avoid the frustration of sticking muffins, I cut squares of parchment paper and used them to line the muffin tins (no sticking).

A nice change from sweet zucchini muffins. To lower the fat content, I used canola oil, less cheese and bacon. I also added more seasonings such as garlic powder, onion powder and Italian seasoning. I baked them at a little higher heat for 20 minutes. Will make again.

Pretty good overall. I reduced the flour to 1 1/2 cups and added 1/2 cup corn meal. I also squeezed the grated zucchini between paper towels to reduce the liquid. The muffins came out crispy on the outside and tender on the inside. They made a nice addition to our supper of white chicken chili. My family loved them!

We really liked these! Light, fluffy & moist. Since I bake a lot with zucchini, my tip is to make sure that ALL the ingredients are at room temperature! This includes the zukes and cheese.

Changes I made are: used 1 cup all purpose and 3/4 cup whole wheat flour (didn't feel like doing the math); used 3/4 cup finely diced ham (had some that needed to be used)that I sauteed in the butter, adding garlic for the last minute or so. I added this directly to the milk/egg mixture, which was not according to the recipe. Also threw in a couple of finely sliced green onions and a sprinkle of chipotle chile powder.

My next batch will omit the garlic, use either bacon or ham, and add more onion as well as possibly black pepper and some herbs.

Has anyone frozen these? I'd like to keep these on hand for breakfast. Great recipe. Thank you!

I was looking for a savory muffin to use some hot country sausage and my abundant zucchini in a new way. This recipe was perfect! I subbed hot country sausage (about 1 cup browned, crumbled sausage), upped the grated parmesan to one cup, and eliminated the grated cheddar. The result was marvelous. Really good recipe!

I made this recipe yesterday, but with a few tweeks. After reading the many reviews about it being bland, i added fresh thyme to the batter. Also, i made sure to get an extra old cheddar cheese. Finally, i put chopped ham instead of bacon. The results-amazing! I had bought jalapeno to use, but forgot to add it. Im sure with that too, it would have been even better. As for the cooking time, 30 minutes is great-but dont open the oven door before! Make sure to put on a cooing rack for ten minutes or so as well. Hope this review was helpful!
I think the zucchini needs to be squeezed of all its moisture perhaps? These are sloppy inside and rubbery on the outside.

I loved this recipe. I didn't have any milk, so I used sour cream. I used a combination of carrots and zucchini and I did drain them. I also used considerably more cheese than the recipe called for, including bacon jalapeno cheddar. I think they turned out fantastic. (in the picture, they are the muffins nearest the camera)

Did this doubled with the following changes - 1/2 cheddar + 1/2 pepper jack because that's what I had, no bacon because vegetarian, and bread pans instead of muffin tins. Came out great and really good as breakfast put through the toaster twice. Partner says 'I like not knowing whether I'm eating bread or a block of cheese.'

I really like these muffins. I didn't pay attention to the recipe and used paper liners. The muffins did stick to the liners probably because of the cheese. So next time will use spray on my muffin tins. I will make them again!

We all did everything as the recipe, but as a result, as with someone's comment, it was the worst finish with a bitter finish. I don't want to make it again. I should have read the comments of others first. I wonder why this recipe is introduced in AllRecipe.

I followed this recipe exactly, including all the ingredients being at room temperature. Both my husband and myself are experienced bakers. The ingredients looked promising but ended up being a disappointment. These had zero flavor, we couldn't even taste the cheese. We ended up trashing the remaining 11 muffins. We won't be making these again.
These are moist and flavorful. They definitely should be eaten warmed up.
We loved them. I did use a half cup more zucchini and I doubled the garlic and bacon.
I made this exactly the way it Pam wrote it and they turned out fantastic! They are great with my morning oatmeal. Thanks Pam!!
More of a biscuit type of muffin. I added extra bacon and used garlic salt instead. Very yummy!

These are delicious! I don't know what happened with others to result in the low ratings. I followed the recipe exactly except for omitting the bacon. They were perfectly done in 30 minutes. They are a bit of a surprise because they have a very different texture and flavor than a breakfast muffin. They will be great with my country steak!
Disappointed after all the prep work and expense they were bland but a bit too salty. Weird crumb and stuck to muffin liners. Still good enough for the family not company.
